situation:
You are the marketing manager for HARROW LANE VINTAGE, an established vintage clothing resale shop that has taken clothing on consignment from the same neighborhood for nineteen years. The owner (judge) has watched the shop lose share since THREADLOOP, an app-based resale entrant, opened the same market to anyone with a phone.

Nearly everything the shop knows about its stock is recorded in the receiving process, where each consigned item is photographed, measured, tagged, and priced before it reaches the floor. The consignment agreement every consignor signs promises that consignor names and item sale records stay confidential and are never handed to another company, and the consignors who have signed it supply the whole floor.

LOOMLIST, a national resale marketplace, will list HARROW LANE's whole floor and put it in front of the shoppers THREADLOOP took. Its supplier contract requires the shop to hand over buyer contact records and item-level purchase histories, which is what the confidentiality clause in the consignment agreement forbids the shop to share.

The other course is a stripped-down site of the shop's own, built only from the photos, measurements, and prices already captured at receiving, with no customer accounts at all. It keeps the confidentiality clause intact and could open within weeks, but it collects almost no data about who buys what and reaches far fewer shoppers than LOOMLIST.

The owner (judge) wants your analysis of what marketing data the shop genuinely needs, how it would be collected under each course of action, and a recommendation on which course to take. The owner (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of HARROW LANE VINTAGE. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have run the shop for nineteen years on consignment from the neighborhood, and you are losing share to THREADLOOP. You want to hear whether the marketing manager recommends listing the floor on LOOMLIST under its supplier contract or opening the shop's own stripped-down site, and you want to hear what the shop looks like some way down the road once that recommendation has been in force.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Six months in, what changes at the receiving desk because of this?
After a year of it, how do the consignors deal with us differently?
